name: proportionality
wording: How much ceremony a change gets, sized to its risk, which its story states as the path it takes and roughly what it will cost. A change that alters no meaning is a task with no story. A story on the plain path is broken into tasks, each built by one builder and reviewed by one reviewer. A story whose risk warrants more scales up with specialists: the architect calls the illustrator, who writes its examples cold, and holds some of them back for review only; the lead calls the check-writer, whose checks are seen failing before the build, and adds a second reviewer or asks the operator to review. So the method never costs more than the change.
reason: The operator, 2026-10-15: the workflow becomes intent-based delegation instead of a prescribed procedure; each role is defined by what it receives and hands over, each handover states what it must contain, and established practice is named rather than restated. A story, not a cut, now carries the ceremony, and the specialists are called in only when its risk warrants them.
